stories.head: Russia's GPS jamming returns to pre-2024 levels
stories.body: Russia's GPS jamming in the Eastern Mediterranean has ramped back up to levels not seen since before 2024, creating navigational chaos just when we thought we had a handle on it. This resurgence raises questions about the operational readiness of global navigation systems, particularly for military applications. Insurers are already rethinking their risk assessments in light of these developments.
stories.soWhat: If you thought GPS was foolproof, think again—this is a reminder that geopolitical tensions can disrupt even the most mundane of technologies.

stories.head: Quantum Space sets sail for SPAC deal
stories.body: Quantum Space has announced plans to go public via a SPAC, a move that values the company at approximately $1.2 billion. This deal comes as the market for space-related companies shows signs of life, despite the general malaise in tech IPOs. Investors are hoping Quantum's maneuverability translates into stock performance, but history suggests caution.
stories.soWhat: The SPAC craze isn’t dead yet, but investors should remember that not all spacecraft make it to orbit—some just burn up on re-entry.

stories.head: U.S. adds $1.4B for space resilience in FY27 budget
stories.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, reflecting a growing recognition that space is a critical national asset. This funding is aimed at bolstering defense capabilities against emerging threats, particularly in light of recent Russian activities. The allocation signals a shift towards prioritizing long-term strategic investments over short-term fixes.
stories.soWhat: More money for space resilience means more contracts for defense contractors—but it also means more scrutiny on how that money is spent.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
